source.author: K. M. de Silva
source.title: A History of Sri Lanka
source.publisher: London: C. Hurst & Company; Berkeley and Los Angeles: University of California Press

note: Read chapter by chapter by Claude from the scan's OCR; years, figures and doubtful readings were cross-checked against a second OCR. Descriptions are summaries, not quotations.

people.name: A. E. Goonesinha
people.description: Most prominent active member of the Young Lanka League; detained in 1915; pioneer of mass politics based on the Colombo working class.

people.name: A. F. Molamure
people.description: Prominent Kandyan member of the Congress who joined the demand for separate Kandyan representation after 1924.

people.name: A. G. Fraser
people.description: Principal of Trinity College, Kandy, who in April 1919 made what was in effect the first call for manhood suffrage.

people.name: A. G. Ranasinha
people.description: Senanayake's adviser on the 1945 mission to London.

people.name: A. M. Ferguson
people.description: With John Ferguson, proprietor of The Ceylon Observer, which opposed abolition of the grain taxes.

people.name: A. Mahadeva
people.description: Tamil politician, son of Sir Ponnambalam Arunachalam; elected Minister of Home Affairs in place of Jayatilaka.

people.name: A. Pavilioen
people.description: Commandeur of Jaffnapatam whose 1665 memoir stated that natives were governed by local custom where clear and reasonable.

people.name: A. R. Buultjens
people.description: Administrator of the Theosophical Society's Buddhist schools.

people.name: Admiral de la Haye
people.description: Commander of the French squadron that appeared off the east coast of Ceylon and entrenched itself at Kottiyar before being driven out by the Dutch.

people.name: Admiral Suffren
people.description: French admiral who captured Trincomalee from the British in August 1782.

people.name: Adrian de Abrew Rajapakse
people.description: Salagama scholar made Maha Mudaliyar in early British times, holding the post jointly with Conrad Peter Dias.

people.name: Afonso de Noronha
people.description: Portuguese viceroy who led the expeditionary force to Sri Lanka in 1550-51. Named only 'de Noronha' in the text; the index conflates him with Constantine de Sa de Noronha.

people.name: Aggabodhi I
people.description: Moriya king, 571-604.

people.name: Aggabodhi II
people.description: Moriya king, 604-14.

people.name: Aggabodhi III
people.description: King (628, 629-39) dependent on South Indian mercenaries.

people.name: Aggabodhi IV
people.description: King (667-83) in whose reign the Madirigiriya vatadage was built.

people.name: Ahalepola
people.description: Nephew and successor of Pilima Talauve as First Adigar; dismissed in early 1814, failed to raise Sabaragamuva, fled to the British and helped plan the 1815 invasion; detained at Colombo from 2 March 1818.

people.name: Akaragama Appuhamy
people.description: Leader of a revolt against the Portuguese in Kotte in 1594.

people.name: Alagiyavanna
people.description: Sixteenth-century poet, the last substantial figure in the classical Sinhalese literary tradition.

people.name: Alakesvara
people.description: Descendant of Nissanka Alagakkonara, minister who defeated the Jaffna forces and became de facto ruler under Bhuvanekabahu V.

roles.title: Chief minister and de facto ruler

people.name: Alaungsithu
people.description: Burmese king who obstructed Sri Lanka's South-East Asian trade, provoking Parakramabahu I's expedition.

people.name: Alexander Johnston
people.description: Chief Justice of Ceylon; guiding influence behind the Charter of Justice of 1810 and trial by jury, and a patron of the parish schools.

people.name: Ambalavanar Kanagasabhai
people.description: Tamil representative in the Legislative Council after Rockwood.

people.name: Ambanvalarala
people.description: Leader of the major rebellion of 1664 against Rajasimha II in the Kandyan kingdom.

people.name: Amoghavajra
people.description: Exponent of Tantric Buddhism who visited the island in the eighth century.

people.name: Anagarika Dharmapala
people.description: Most militant and charismatic of the Buddhist 'nationalist' leaders; early advocate of swaraj and of Sinhalese-Buddhist dominance; often abroad, and kept out of Ceylon from 1914 to 1920. Brother of Edmund and Dr C. A. Hewavitharane.

people.name: Ananda Coomaraswamy
people.description: Orientalist; leader with Arunachalam of the 'university movement'.

people.name: Ananda Rajakaruna
people.description: Sinhalese neo-classical poet.

people.name: Anauratha
people.description: King of Burma who gave economic aid to Vijayabahu I.

people.name: Andre Furtado de Mendoca
people.description: Commander of the Portuguese expedition to Jaffna in 1591.

people.name: Andrew Nichol
people.description: British water-colourist, the first serious painter in the medium to work in Ceylon; in charge of the School of Design at the Colombo Academy in the 1840s.

roles.title: Head of the School of Design

people.name: Antonio Barretto
people.description: Leader of revolts against the Portuguese in 1603 and 1616-19 (indexed in the book also as Antonio Barretto).

places.name: Uva
places.note: Disava of Uva, early seventeenth century.

people.name: Arabi Pasha
people.description: Leader of the abortive Egyptian uprising of 1882, exiled to Ceylon 1883-1901, where he promoted English education and religious reform among Muslims.

people.name: Arthur Creech-Jones
people.description: Hall's successor as Secretary of State for the Colonies; receptive to Dominion Status for Ceylon.

roles.title: Secretary of State for the Colonies

people.name: Arumuga Navalar
people.description: Dominant figure of the nineteenth-century Hindu (Saivite) revival among the Tamils of Jaffna: scholar and editor of classical Tamil texts, pamphleteer, orator, founder of schools, a press and Saivite societies; no social reformer.

people.name: Aryacakravarti
people.description: Leader of a Pandyan army installed as ruler of Jaffna; founder of the Aryacakravarti line.

people.name: Asoka
people.description: Mauryan emperor, convert to and patron of Buddhism, contemporary and ally of Devanampiya Tissa.

people.name: Aung San
people.description: Leader of Burma's independence struggle, assassinated with his closest associates on 19 June 1947.

people.name: Badiuddin Mahmud
people.description: S.L.F.P. Muslim politician, Minister of Education in Mrs Bandaranaike's first government and again in the United Front government, who drew Muslim support to the S.L.F.P.

people.name: Bailey
people.description: British official, author of a Report on Irrigation in Uva (1859).

people.name: Bhalluka
people.description: Dravidian adventurer named with Elara among those who tried to seize power.

people.name: Bhuvanekabahu I
people.description: Sinhalese king who sent a mission to the Egyptian court.

people.name: Bhuvanekabahu IV
people.description: King at Gampola under whom Lankatilaka and Gadaladeniya were completed.

people.name: Bhuvanekabahu V
people.description: Gampola king who fled before a Jaffna attack; last ruler of his line.

people.name: Bhuvanekabahu VII
people.description: Eldest son of Vijayabahu VI; king of the truncated Kotte kingdom and Portuguese client, shot dead by a Portuguese soldier.

people.name: Birch
people.description: Civil servant who supplied Ward with data and ideas for his irrigation programme.

people.name: Bowles Daly
people.description: Manager of Buddhist schools under the Theosophical Society.

people.name: Brigadier-General de Meuron
people.description: Head of the Committee of Investigation that administered the maritime provinces from June 1797 to 12 November 1798.

people.name: Buddha
people.description: Founder of Buddhism, born in North India around 563 BC.

people.name: Buddhadatta
people.description: Fifth-century Pali commentator, not a native of the island.

people.name: Buddhaghosa
people.description: Fifth-century Brahman (probably South Indian) convert, Mahavihara scholar, author of the Visuddhimagga and Pali commentaries.

people.name: Bussy
people.description: French commander whose expedition to India failed (1782-83).

people.name: C. A. Bonjean
people.description: Roman Catholic prelate who led the Catholic challenge to Protestant mission dominance in education.

people.name: C. A. Hewavitharane
people.description: Physician, brother of the Anagarika Dharmapala; detained in 1915.

people.name: C. Batuwantudawe
people.description: Temperance leader detained in 1915.

people.name: C. E. Victor Corea
people.description: Militant nationalist who consistently supported Goonesinha and the strikers in 1923.

people.name: C. H. Cameron
people.description: Second member of the Commission of Eastern Inquiry, a dogmatic Utilitarian whose report on the judiciary was the basis of the Charter of Justice of 1833.

people.name: C. H. de Soysa
people.description: Karava magnate backed by the press for the post of Maha Mudaliyar in 1884.

people.name: C. J. R. Le Mesurier
people.description: Assistant Government Agent of Nuvara Eliya whose 1888 administration report disclosed that 1,048 villagers had starved in Valapane in 1882-5 after evictions for grain-tax arrears.

places.name: Nuvara Eliya
places.note: Assistant Government Agent

people.name: C. P. de Silva
people.description: Deputy to Mrs Bandaranaike in the S.L.F.P. who crossed over to the Opposition with a group of followers and brought down her government at the end of 1964.

people.name: C. V. Brayne
people.description: British official who devised the peasant proprietor system of restricted leasehold tenure in Batticaloa in the 1920s; member of the Land Commission.

people.name: C. W. Leadbeater
people.description: Theosophist who accompanied Olcott in 1886 and helped run the Buddhist schools.

people.name: C. W. W. Kannangara
people.description: Member of the Board of Ministers reported in December 1938 to belong to the Sinhala Maha Sabha.

people.name: Cankili Kumara
people.description: Nephew of Ethirimanna Cinkam who seized power in Jaffna in 1615 and ruled as regent until captured by the Portuguese in 1619.

places.name: Jaffna
places.note: as regent

people.name: Chandrabhanu
people.description: Ruler of Tambralinga (the 'Javaka' king) who invaded Sri Lanka in 1247, later ruled Jaffna and was killed in a second invasion.

places.name: Jaffna
places.note: as tributary of the Pandyas

people.name: Charles Bruce
people.description: Official who drafted the island's Revised Education Code in the 1880s, aiming primary schooling at the village child's 'humble career'.

roles.title: Official; drafter of the Revised Education Code

people.name: Charles Dias
people.description: Leading nationalist playwright of the Sinhalese urban (Tower Hall) theatre.

people.name: Cheng-ho
people.description: Ming admiral who led seven naval expeditions into the Indian Ocean.

people.name: Christopher Elliott
people.description: Physician and outspoken journalist who led the radical agitation for a representative Legislative Council in the 1840s.

people.name: Clement Attlee
people.description: British Prime Minister in the Labour government of 1945.

people.name: Colonel Seely
people.description: Crewe's Parliamentary Under-Secretary at the Colonial Office; co-initiator of the 1910 concession.

people.name: Conrad Peter Dias
people.description: Member of the goyigama establishment who held the post of Maha Mudaliyar jointly with Adrian de Abrew Rajapakse.

people.name: Constantine de Sa
people.description: Portuguese Captain-General in Sri Lanka; his army was destroyed at Randenivela in 1630.

people.name: Cosmas
people.description: Author of the Christian Topography, source for Sri Lanka's role as an Indian Ocean entrepot.

people.name: D. B. Jayatilaka
people.description: Buddhist temperance leader detained in 1915; spent three years in England on the post-riots campaign; retired from active politics in 1942.

roles.title: Ceylon Government Representative in New Delhi

people.name: D. C. Senanayake
people.description: Son of Don Spater Senanayake, active in the temperance movement; detained in 1915.

people.name: D. J. Gogerly
people.description: Wesleyan missionary whose tactical and administrative skill secured official adoption of vernacular education in 1843-8.

people.name: D. S. Senanayake
people.description: Temperance leader, son of Don Spater Senanayake; detained in 1915.

people.name: Dathopatissa I
people.description: King c. 639-50, dependent on South Indian mercenaries.

people.name: Devanampiya Tissa
people.description: King at Anuradhapura, 250-210 BC, under whom Buddhism was introduced; granted the park that became the Mahavihara.

people.name: Devaragampola Silvatanna
people.description: Unordained monk and the most distinguished painter of the Kandyan school; painted Degaldoruva and the Ridi vihara in 1771-6.

people.name: Dhammakitti
people.description: Bhikkhu to whom the thirteenth-century Culavamsa is attributed.

people.name: Dhammapala
people.description: Pali commentator, not a native of the island.

people.name: Dharma Parakramabahu IX
people.description: King of Kotte who ended the Pitigal-Alutkuru rebellion.

people.name: Dharmapala
people.description: Grandson and heir of Bhuvanekabahu; Catholic king of Kotte under Portuguese tutelage who bequeathed his kingdom to Portugal.

people.name: Dhatusena
people.description: Moriya prince who expelled South Indian invaders; king 455-73; murdered by his son Kassapa.

people.name: Diederik van Domburg
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1734-1736, under whom unrest in the low-country worsened.

people.name: Don Spater Senanayake
people.description: Plumbago magnate behind the Hapitigam temperance societies; father of F. R., D. S. and D. C. Senanayake.

people.name: Donald Obeysekera
people.description: Leading light of the Ceylon Unionist Association.

people.name: Dr Drummond Shiels
people.description: Most active member of the Donoughmore Commission and patron of Goonesinha; Under-Secretary at the India Office (June-November 1929) and at the Colonial Office (1 December 1929-31 August 1931).

people.name: Dudley Senanayake
people.description: Leader, with J. R. Jayewardene, of the younger Congressmen who framed the party programme of 1939.

people.name: Dutthagamani
people.description: Son and successor of Kavantissa; defeated Elara and first unified the island under one ruler.

people.name: E. F. C. Ludowyk
people.description: Professor of English at the University of Ceylon whose productions of Western classics set the pace for university theatre in the 1940s.

people.name: E. J. Samarawickreme
people.description: President of the Ceylon Reform League in 1918; co-signatory of the pledge to the Jaffna Association.

people.name: E. L. Mitford
people.description: Official whose memoranda on 'serfdom' (December 1868, January 1869) argued for immediate compulsory abolition of service tenures in temple villages.

people.name: E. R. Sarachchandra
people.description: Sinhalese literary critic and later dramatist; author of Modern Sinhalese Fiction and The Folk Drama of Ceylon; adapted Western classics and folk drama for the Sinhalese stage.

people.name: E. W. Perera
people.description: Sinhalese Christian reform leader who spent four years in England (from 1915) seeking an inquiry into the suppression of the riots.

people.name: Earl Grey
people.description: Secretary of State for the Colonies 1846-52; free trader; reaffirmed dissociation from Buddhism in 1847.

roles.title: Secretary of State for the Colonies
Secretary of State for the Colonies

people.name: Earl of Donoughmore
people.description: Chairman of the Special Commission on Constitutional Reform.

people.name: Edirille rala
people.description: Leader of a revolt against the Portuguese in Kotte, 1594-6.

people.name: Edmund Hewavitharane
people.description: Brother of the Anagarika Dharmapala; detained in 1915.

people.name: Edward Barnes
people.description: Governor whose system of roads first broke the isolation of the Kandyan region.

places.name: Ceylon
places.note: Named as Governor in 1824; tenure dates not given in this chapter.

places.name: Ceylon
places.note: Road-builder of the 1820s.

people.name: Edward Gibbon Wakefield
people.description: Theorist of colonisation whose doctrines on land prices guided the Colonial Office's crown land sales policy.

people.name: Edward VII
people.description: British king whose coronation in 1902 was the occasion for Ferguson's reform initiative.

people.name: Edwin Montagu
people.description: Secretary of State for India, author of the declaration of 20 August 1917.

people.name: Elara
people.description: South Indian ruler at Anuradhapura from 145 BC, reputed for justice; killed by Dutthagamani.

places.name: Anuradhapura
places.note: usurper

people.name: Ethirimanna Cinkam
people.description: King of Jaffna installed by the Portuguese in 1591; died 1615.

people.name: F. J. de Mel
people.description: Author of a 1907 article on reform of the Ceylon Legislative Council.

people.name: F. R. Dias Bandaranaike
people.description: The most powerful S.L.F.P. cabinet minister in the United Front government; joined the campaign to postpone the 1977 elections in September 1976.

people.name: F. R. Senanayake
people.description: Temperance leader, son of Don Spater Senanayake; detained in 1915; with Jayatilaka set the restrained tone of the Buddhist movement from about 1918.

people.name: Fa Hsien
people.description: Chinese Buddhist traveller who lived in the island in the fifth century and described Anuradhapura's merchants.

people.name: Filipe de Oliveira
people.description: Commander of the Portuguese conquest of Jaffna in 1619.

people.name: Francis de Zoysa
people.description: Congress leader who insisted on demanding immediate responsible government.

people.name: Frederick North
people.description: First British Governor of the maritime provinces, appointed 12 October 1798 under Dual Control; conservative restorer of headmen, rajakariya and caste, experimenter in land registration, and advocate of permanent British possession and a separate civil service.

places.name: Ceylon
places.note: 'Governor North'; dates not given in this chapter.

places.name: Ceylon
places.note: Dates not given in this chapter.

people.name: G. B. Senanayake
people.description: Sinhalese short-story writer and literary critic.

people.name: G. C. S. Corea
people.description: Member of the November 1940 delegation to New Delhi.

roles.title: Minister of Labour, Industry and Commerce

people.name: G. E. Madawala
people.description: Kandyan lawyer, member of the 1920 Kandyan delegation to London.

people.name: G. G. Ponnambalam
people.description: Young Tamil orator, member of the Liberal League, elected to the State Council for Point Pedro in 1934 and soon leader of the Tamils.

people.name: G. H. Hall
people.description: Labour Secretary of State for the Colonies from the 1945 change of government.

roles.title: Secretary of State for the Colonies

people.name: G. H. Perera
people.description: Sinhalese neo-classical poet.

people.name: Gajabahu I
people.description: King who enlarged the Abhayagiri stupa in the second century AD.

people.name: Gajabahu II
people.description: Ruler at Polonnaruva before Parakramabahu I.

people.name: Gandhi
people.description: Indian leader under whose influence the Indian National Congress was coming; inspiration of the Young Lanka League's swaraj ideal.

people.name: General MacDowall
people.description: British general who led the embassy to Kandy and commanded the 1803 expedition until illness forced him back to Colombo.

people.name: George Keyt
people.description: Painter who fused the tradition of Picasso with Hindu mythology; the one major artistic talent to emerge from the East-West encounter under British rule.

people.name: George VI
people.description: British king whose coronation the L.S.S.P. members opposed celebrating.

people.name: George Wall
people.description: Leading campaigner in Ceylon for abolition of the grain taxes, associated with The Ceylon Independent.

people.name: Gothabhaya
people.description: King (249-62), mildly sympathetic to Mahayanism.

people.name: Gregory de Zoysa
people.description: Salagama; in 1845 the first non-goyigama appointed mudaliyar of the Governor's Gate.

people.name: Gurulugomi
people.description: Thirteenth-century Sinhalese prose author of the Amavatura and Dharmapradipikava.

people.name: Gustaaf Willem van Imhoff
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon from July 1736 (to 1740); sought conciliation with Kandy, opened cinnamon-reserve land to coconut and coffee, extended the canal system and proposed making Ceylon a trade emporium.

places.name: Maritime provinces
places.note: Term dates from the book's list of governors (van Imhoff: 1736-40 per the text, 1736-9 per the list)

people.name: H. A. P. Sandarasagara
people.description: Tamil politician who threatened to make Jaffna 'an Ulster'.

people.name: H. J. C. Pereira
people.description: Leader of the movement for constitutional reform, attached to British institutions.

people.name: H. J. Huxham
people.description: Financial Secretary of Ceylon; member of the November 1940 delegation to New Delhi.

people.name: H. R. Cowell
people.description: Colonial Office official who minuted on the Jaffna seats on 30 May 1933.

people.name: Harry Creasy
people.description: Respected English resident and European representative in the Legislative Council who supported Ramanathan after the riots.

people.name: Hendrik Becker
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon who found senior Company officials at Galle engaged in illegal private trade in cloth.

places.name: Ceylon
places.note: Dates not given in the book.

people.name: Henry Dundas
people.description: President of the Board of Control for India; devised the Dual Control compromise, later decided to separate Ceylon from the Company, opposed the peace treaty and resigned.

people.name: Henry Steel Olcott
people.description: American founder (1875) of the Theosophical Society; visited Ceylon in 1880, 1884 and 1886; started the Buddhist education movement, the Vesak holiday agitation and the Buddhist flag.

people.name: Hugh Boyd
people.description: English East India Company envoy on the second British mission to Kandy, 1782.

people.name: Hyder Ali
people.description: Indian ruler whose attacks, with those of the French, shook British power in South India in 1780-82.

people.name: Iman Willem Falck
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1765-1785; pioneered cinnamon plantations, thunhavul land grants, concessions to the salagamas and completed the cadastral survey (thombos).

people.name: J. A. Halangoda
people.description: Kandyan lawyer, author of 'Present Politics and the Rights of the Kandyans' (1920) and member of the Kandyan delegation to Milner.

people.name: J. L. K. van Dort
people.description: Burgher painter, the one superior talent of the wave of popular painting launched by Nichol.

people.name: J. P. Obeysekere
people.description: Sinhalese representative in the Legislative Council, from the hard core of the traditional elite; a strong supporter of Bruce's restrictive Revised Education Code.

people.name: J. R. Jayewardene
people.description: Leader, with Dudley Senanayake, of the younger Congressmen who framed the party programme of 1939.

people.name: J. Vijayatunga
people.description: Journalist and author of Grass for my Feet (London, 1933), vignettes of the rural south.

people.name: Jacob Christiaan Pielat
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1732-1734, instructed by Batavia to tell the Kandyan court that the ports would never be re-opened.

people.name: Jacob de Mel
people.description: Father-in-law of James Pieris; his daughter was an heiress.

people.name: Jacome Goncalves
people.description: Konkani Brahman Catholic priest from Goa who, from refuge in the Kandyan kingdom, produced a large body of Christian literature in Sinhalese and Tamil.

people.name: James Alexander Stewart Mackenzie
people.description: Governor of Ceylon 1837-41; promoted Christian conversion, broke Anglican control of the School Commission and advocated vernacular education.

people.name: James Alwis
people.description: Sinhalese representative in the Legislative Council who supported the administration's retention of the grain taxes.

people.name: James Cordiner
people.description: Clergyman, North's confidant and associate in maintaining the parish schools.

roles.title: Clergyman in charge of parish schools

people.name: James Pieris
people.description: Karava lawyer, Cambridge double first and President of the Union; son-in-law of Jacob de Mel; karava-backed candidate for the Sinhalese seat in 1900 and 1905; more engaged in business and planting than politics at this time.

people.name: James Stephen
people.description: Permanent Under-Secretary at the Colonial Office, who called the Charter of Justice of 1833 'a pure invention ... based on speculation'.

people.name: James Stuart
people.description: Colonel (later General), Andrews' superior in the island, who predicted that the reforms would cause rebellion.

roles.title: Colonel; senior British officer in the island

people.name: Jan Schreuder
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1757-1762 whose harsh land measures provoked the rebellion of 1757 in the south-west.

places.name: Maritime provinces
places.note: Term dates from the book's list of governors (van Imhoff: 1736-40 per the text, 1736-9 per the list)

people.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
people.description: Prime Minister of India; party to the Nehru-Kotelawala pact of 1954 on Indians in Ceylon.

people.name: Jayavira
people.description: Son of Senasammata Vikramabahu; ruler of the Udarata who helped the Kotte princes in 1521 and was expelled by his son.

people.name: Jeremy Bentham
people.description: Utilitarian thinker whose speculations, according to James Stephen, underlay the Charter of Justice of 1833.

people.name: Jeronimo de Azevedo
people.description: Portuguese Captain-General in Sri Lanka who proclaimed Portuguese sovereignty over Kotte in 1597 and waged destructive forays against Kandy.

people.name: Jeronis de Soysa
people.description: Karava from Moratuva, the wealthiest Sinhalese of his day; appointed mudaliyar of the Governor's Gate in 1853 over goyigama opposition.

people.name: Joao III
people.description: King of Portugal who crowned a golden statue of Dharmapala in 1543.

people.name: Joao IV
people.description: First Braganza king of Portugal, restored 1640.

people.name: Johan Gerard van Angelbeek
people.description: Last Dutch governor of Ceylon (1793-5 in the text; 1794-6 in the book's list), successor and father-in-law of de Graaf.

places.name: Maritime provinces
places.note: List of governors gives 1794-6

people.name: Johan Gideon Loten
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1752-1757 who re-imposed restraints on peasant agriculture to protect cinnamon.

places.name: Maritime provinces
places.note: Term dates from the book's list of governors (van Imhoff: 1736-40 per the text, 1736-9 per the list)

people.name: John D'Oyly
people.description: British expert on Kandyan affairs who ran the intelligence network, negotiated with the chiefs and largely drafted the Kandyan Convention.

roles.title: Resident in the Kandyan provinces
roles.organization: Board of Commissioners of Kandyan Affairs

people.name: John de Silva
people.description: Leading nationalist playwright of the Sinhalese urban (Tower Hall) theatre.

people.name: John Ferguson
people.description: With A. M. Ferguson, proprietor of The Ceylon Observer, which opposed abolition of the grain taxes.

people.name: John Frederick Dickson
people.description: First Government Agent of the North-Central Province, at whose suggestion the village tank repair experiment began. (The book gives only 'Mr Dickson'.)

places.name: North-Central Province
places.note: first Government Agent

people.name: John Pybus
people.description: Envoy of the Madras establishment of the English East India Company who led its first diplomatic mission to the Kandyan court in 1762.

people.name: John Rodney
people.description: Chief Secretary of the colony 1806-33, described by the author as incompetent; under him the office declined in importance.

people.name: Joseph Chamberlain
people.description: Secretary of State for the Colonies, recipient of Havelock's confidential despatch of 20 October 1895.

roles.title: Secretary of State for the Colonies

people.name: Jotiya Sitana
people.description: Leader of an insurrection in the Udarata late in Parakramabahu VI's reign.

people.name: Julius Stein van Gollenesse
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1743-1751; continued van Imhoff's land and trade liberalisation, let Muslims and Chetties own land (1746) and tried to manipulate Kandyan court factions.

places.name: Ceylon
places.note: End year from footnoted Memoir title (1743-1751).

places.name: Maritime provinces
places.note: Term dates from the book's list of governors (van Imhoff: 1736-40 per the text, 1736-9 per the list)

people.name: Justin Daraniyagala
people.description: One of the two outstanding Sri Lankan painters of the first half of the twentieth century.

people.name: K. Natesa Iyer
people.description: Former colleague of Goonesinha who became leader of the Indian workers in Colombo and pioneer organiser of plantation labour.

people.name: Kamaladevi Chattopadhaya
people.description: Indian politician who presided over the Jaffna Youth League's annual meeting in April 1931.

people.name: Kangara arachchi
people.description: Leader of a revolt against the Portuguese in 1603.

people.name: Kappitipola
people.description: Disava of Uva and brother-in-law of Ahalepola; went over to the rebels in November 1817 and led the rebellion; later captured.

people.name: Karaliyadde Bandara

people.description: Brother-in-law of Kavantissa, ruler of the small kingdom of Giri, later at Soma.

people.name: Sri Mara Sri Vallabha
people.description: Pandyan king (815-60) who invaded Sri Lanka.

people.name: Sri Rahula Maha Sthavira
people.description: Most distinguished bhikkhu and scholar of the Kotte kingdom; author of the Paravi and Salalihini sandesas.

people.name: Sri Vallabha
people.description: Great-grandson of Mitta and son of Manabharana; exiled claimant whose invasion from the Cola country failed.

people.name: Sri Vijaya Rajasimha
people.description: First Nayakkar king of Kandy, brother of Narendrasimha's chief queen; acceded in 1739.

people.name: Sri Vikrama Rajasimha
people.description: Last Nayakkar king of Kandy and last king in Sri Lanka's history (early nineteenth century); appointed a third adigar and revived the marala death duty.

places.note: Last king; early nineteenth century.

people.name: T. B. Jayah
people.description: Muslim representative in the Legislative Council; author of the memorandum of 27 July 1930.

people.name: T. B. Kobbakaduva
people.description: Prominent Kandyan member of the Congress who demanded separate Kandyan representation after 1924.

people.name: T. B. L. Moonemalle
people.description: Kandyan lawyer, member of the 1920 Kandyan delegation to London.

people.name: T. B. Panabokke
people.description: Appointed Kandyan member of the enlarged Legislative Council in 1889; outspoken critic of the grain taxes.

people.name: Thomas Maitland
people.description: Governor of Ceylon from 1805, Brownrigg's predecessor; abandoned the border raids and kept strictly on the defensive towards Kandy.

people.name: Thomas Ralph Blackhouse
people.description: Collector of Mannar 1820-3; the first British official to visit Anuradhapura (1823).

places.name: Mannar
places.note: Collector of Mannar

people.name: Thome de Sousa
people.description: Portuguese commander who devastated the Devundara devale in 1588.

people.name: Tilak
people.description: Champion of the Hindu resurgence in Western India, to whose propaganda Dharmapala's is compared.

people.name: Tipu Sahib
people.description: The most formidable of the Indian rulers opposing the British; possible recipient of French support via Dutch Ceylon.

people.name: Tudor Rajapakse
people.description: Leading light of the Ceylon Unionist Association.

people.name: Upatissa II
people.description: Lambakanna king, 517-18.

people.name: Vajrabodhi
people.description: Exponent of Tantric Buddhism who visited the island in the eighth century.

people.name: Valivita Saranankara
people.description: Buddhist monk (1698-1778), founder of the Silvat Samagama and leader of the Kandyan Buddhist and literary revival; made sangharaja.

people.name: Vasabha
people.description: Founder of the first Lambakanna dynasty; king AD 67-111.

people.name: Vattagamani
people.description: King of Anuradhapura in whose time further Dravidian adventurers seized power.

people.name: Vattavethera
people.description: Monk traditionally credited with the Guttila da kava.

people.name: Vidiye Bandara
people.description: Son-in-law of Bhuvanekabahu and father of Dharmapala; regent of Kotte, then rebel against the Portuguese.

people.name: Vijaya
people.description: Legendary founding father of the Sinhalese in the Mahavamsa; banished from Sihapura with 700 followers.

people.name: Vijayabahu I
people.description: King (1055-1110) who restored the sangha with monks from Burma.

people.name: Vijayabahu II
people.description: Successor of Parakramabahu I by seniority; kept friendly relations with Burma.

people.name: Vijayabahu III
people.description: First Dambadeniya king.

people.name: Vijayabahu VI
people.description: King of Kotte, unpopular for subservience to the Portuguese; killed by his three elder sons in 1521.

people.name: Vikramabahu II
people.description: Ruler at Polonnaruva before Parakramabahu I, whose legal status as sovereign was not accepted.

people.name: Vikramabahu III
people.description: Gampola king; brother-in-law of Alakesvara.

people.name: Vilbave
people.description: Ex-bhikkhu who posed as the Nayakkar prince Doraisami and was the pretender-king of the 1817-18 rebellion; exposed by the British as an impostor.

people.name: Vimala Dharma Suriya I
people.description: Son of Weerasundera Bandara who fled to the Portuguese and was known as Dom Joao of Austria; later king of Kandy.

people.name: Vimala Dharma Suriya II
people.description: King of Kandy 1687-1707, successor of Rajasimha II; a diffident and pacific ruler who pressed the Dutch to open the ports to Kandyan trade.

people.name: Vira Alakesvara
people.description: Successor of Bhuvanekabahu V as Sinhalese king; captured by Cheng-ho and taken to China.

people.name: Vira Parakramabahu VII
people.description: King of Kotte in whose reign Pitigal and Alutkuru Korales rebelled; numbered VII in the book.

people.name: Virarajendra I
people.description: Cola king (1063-9), son of Rajendra I, under whom Cola power weakened.

people.name: Viscount Castlereagh
people.description: Secretary of State for the Colonies who, under Evangelical pressure, instructed Maitland to promote education.

people.name: Viscount Milner
people.description: Secretary of State for the Colonies who received the Kandyan and Congress delegations in June 1920.

roles.title: Secretary of State for the Colonies

people.name: Viscount Torrington
people.description: Governor of Ceylon whose new taxes, notably the Road Ordinance, provoked the opposition of 1848.

people.name: Voharika Tissa
people.description: King (209-31) who suppressed Mahayanist teachings.

people.name: W. A. de Silva
people.description: Temperance leader detained in 1915.

people.name: W. A. Silva
people.description: Pioneer Sinhalese novelist who stressed literature as entertainment and broke with both classical other-worldliness and Sirisena's didacticism.

people.name: W. Dahanayake
people.description: Minister of Education in S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike's government, who resisted pressure to bring all schools under state control.

people.name: W. G. Rockwood
people.description: Non-vellala Tamil nominated to the Tamil seat in place of Coomaraswamy.

people.name: W. L. Murphy
people.description: Official who wrote for the Colonial Secretary of Ceylon to the Congress on 29 April 1927.

people.name: W. M. G. Colebrooke
people.description: Senior member of the two-member Commission of Eastern Inquiry, whose 1831 reports recommended ending monopolies and rajakariya, a School Commission, Executive and Legislative Councils and a unified administration.

people.name: Waitialingam Duraiswamy
people.description: Influential Jaffna politician who endorsed the Youth League's boycott.

people.name: Walter Pereira
people.description: Leading Sri Lankan lawyer who acted as Attorney General with distinction but was not confirmed in the post.

people.name: Weerasundera Bandara
people.description: Kandyan notable executed by Rajasimha I; father of Konappu Bandara.

people.name: Willem Jacob van de Graaf
people.description: Dutch Governor of Ceylon 1785-1793 (book's spelling: de Graaf); pushed coffee, pepper, cardamom, cotton and indigo, rice production and colonisation schemes, provoking the rebellion of 1789-90.

places.note: List of governors gives 1785-94

people.name: William Digby
people.description: British journalist resident in Ceylon; author of two pamphlets (1876, 1877) arguing for representative government; close friend and correspondent of Arunachalam.

people.name: William Goonetileke
people.description: Goyigama scholar and lawyer without 'first-class' status who contended for the Sinhalese seat in 1878.

people.name: William Ormsby-Gore
people.description: Under-Secretary of State for the Colonies who in February 1927 proposed a commission for Ceylon.

roles.title: Secretary of State for the Colonies

people.name: William Pitt
people.description: British statesman who in 1787 authorised Cornwallis to occupy Trincomalee in case of war with the Dutch.

people.name: William Silva
people.description: Left-wing member of S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike's Cabinet who did not belong to the S.L.F.P.

people.name: William V, Prince of Orange
people.description: Dutch Stadholder, Captain-General and Admiral of Holland, who took asylum in England early in 1795 and issued the Kew Letter. Not named in the book.

people.name: William Willerman
people.description: Able British staff officer responsible for the technical aspects of the 1815 invasion plan.

people.name: Zamorin of Calicut
people.description: Ruler of Calicut on the Malabar coast, naval ally of Mayadunne until 1539.
